_about: Saint Jude's lethality figures (task B12c). Each is a Design proposal with its reasoning in `why`. They lay over engine/lethality_default.json; a null removes a ceiling. Case-fatality rates quoted in `why` (from memory, US, approximate, to be checked) are calibration targets reported after a run, never caps: no figure here clamps a share.

why.owner_rule: Lean toward life governs uncertain survival only, never what violent people choose. When someone means to kill and can, a killing that lands kills.
why.ceilings: The old 0.82 (lethal) and 0.22 (hostile) fatal ceilings are removed (null cap). Severity curves still rise with the wound; they are no longer clamped.
why.methods: Target range of fatal fraction once a blow lands (US, approximate, unverified): beating 1-2%, knife 3-5%, firearm injury overall 15-30%, point-blank shot to head or torso above 70%, execution-style shot near-certain. Floors carry the method's own base lethality because resolved severity (resisted by the victim's resilience) does not describe where the blow fell.
why.hit: A planned hit is a different intent from a beating. Landed at point-blank it kills about 90-95%; the share falls with a low chance of success (a glancing or interrupted blow) and with a guarded target. The chance that it lands at all is the odds the caller computes (strength, stage, guard).
why.nonlethal: A beating-style attack that lands kills rarely (street gangs, which fight with whatever is to hand, more than durable outfits, which send men who know how far to go).
why.internal: A killing the head or a man decides on one of his own through the agenda (an ordered hit, a discipline or held-man killing, killing an offender) lands at `internal.land` and then kills at the planned-hit rate, so the man can survive, hurt or not, knowing who tried (Joe Gallo, Carmine Persico and others survived attempts; an ambush by a trusted man lands more often than a hit on a guarded stranger). The state-changing killings of a coup, contest or war (org_coup, org_succession) stay certain: the code that follows each (succession, books, counts) assumes the man is dead. A reply to a killing across outfits goes against a man who expects it, so each man sent lands 0.7 of the time and then kills at the planned-hit rate; the reply is a team, so one failure does not end it.
why.guard: B13b. A man with many answering to him is harder to reach: `internal.guard_land` takes that share (times how guarded he is, 0..1, from `tension.guard.half`) off the chance a planned blow lands, and `hit.guard_weight` off its being fatal once it lands. Carmine Galante (1979) and Paul Castellano (1985) were reached in the open, outside, with their guards away or not in the room (all [memory], approximate); a boss with his whole outfit around him was seldom reached at all. Design proposal.
why.untreated: A serious wound with no care can worsen (infection, bleeding) and kill weeks later; treatment cuts the worsening. Firearm wounds start worsening at a lower severity than blows.

incident.why: A weekly beating mostly stays a beating, but a share go too far (a weapon, a bad fall, a bystander). The tail share and its severity are proposals; the deaths are reported by the run, never clamped.
